reason: ChartStyle writes its CSS as the <style>'s text, not with dangerouslySetInnerHTML: an App page's frame enforces Trusted Types with no policy, so innerHTML throws. Its surface, which takes keyboard focus (accessibilityLayer), shows a focus ring that upstream hides.
SidebarProvider writes no cookie: an App page's frame has an opaque origin, where document.cookie throws.
A single number value or defaultValue renders one thumb: upstream counts only arrays, so <Slider defaultValue={40} /> drew two.

The day button gets the ref its focus effect reads, which upstream never attaches, so the arrow keys move focus from day to day; and the two String.raw class strings move out of the component, as the React Compiler can't compile a tagged template whose raw text differs from its value.
ToastAction's and ToastClose's default element is chosen in the body, not as the parameter's default: the React Compiler can't compile a JSX default.
A menubar's trigger shows a focus ring when the keyboard reaches it; upstream shows none.
ComboboxInput's trigger and clear buttons are named (Show options, Clear); upstream's are icons with no name.
The orientation reaches Base UI, not only the styles, so a vertical group moves with the up and down arrows.

Its last step completes in an App page's frame, which submits no form and fires no submit event: the form's requestSubmit() fires the submit event itself, and the submit button calls it on its click, so the questionnaire's checks and onSubmit run.
